claims.text: A newly developed computational potential, such as a machine-learning potential, can better represent the atomic configurations of an ab initio liquid in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Better representation of liquid atomic configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed potential can accurately capture the atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid.
The intervention is applicable to equiatomic or near-equiatomic multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The intervention is applicable at temperatures near the alloy melting point.
Relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references, the proposed potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by an estimated 20–50%.
TOR-TILD's EAM references provide the baseline for evaluating the proposed potential.
Molecular-dynamics calculations can compare the proposed potential with TOR-TILD's EAM references using liquid free energies and thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
Failure to obtain more than a 10% reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to the EAM references would falsify the hypothesis.
The exact mismatch reduction and optimal composition and temperature ranges remain uncertain.
